properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-26 on 0.71.0: the merge driver's committed export names ITSELF as its parent (prev_content_hash == content_hash) and carries no taken_at; and fact:the-merge-driver-writes-the-merged-export-in-a-different-byte-layout-than-the-exporter-2026-09-22 recurs unchanged, including `wrote: unchanged` on a write that changed bytes
properties.source: reflow2-mcp 0.71.0 release binary as git merge driver; merges of main into reflow2 PR #595 and flo2 PR #80, 2026-09-26
properties.statement:
OBSERVED twice in one session, merging main into two open PRs after their sibling records PRs had squash-merged (reflow2 #594 then #595; flo2 #79 then #80). Both repos have `.gitattributes` naming the reflow2 driver, configured as the 0.71.0 release binary.

(1) NEW DETAIL. The blob git committed for the merge (flo2 merge f355dbc) had content_hash 788a4e53 AND prev_content_hash 788a4e53, its own hash, and no taken_at key at all. The rebase of #595 onto main committed the same shape (no taken_at). A PR that commits the driver's result without a re-export therefore carries an export whose lineage points at itself and which cannot say what tree it was taken in. Whether the CI design gate refuses that was not tested: every merge here was followed by a re-export before pushing.

(2) RECURRENCE, same as 2026-09-22. `git diff --stat origin/main` read ~54k lines (flo2) and ~420k lines (reflow2) for a design delta of a few hundred. export_graph afterwards reported `wrote: unchanged` with the note "NOTHING WAS WRITTEN — the file already held exactly this design, byte for byte". That is false: `git status --porcelain` was EMPTY straight after the flo2 merge commit and showed ` M docs/design/flo2.json` straight after the export, the diff being prev_content_hash (788a4e53 → a949a287, the records PR's hash) and taken_at added. So `wrote` compares content only, while the note claims bytes.

Workaround used, and it holds: commit the merge, then export_graph (it anchors at the merge-base, which is now main's tip, so it chains one hop from main), then amend the still-unpushed merge commit, then push as a plain fast-forward. Exporting BEFORE committing the merge chains from the OLD merge-base (54c6c049 on reflow2, not #594's 12ba0f90), because HEAD has not moved yet. Not root-caused here.

(3) THE CONVERSE, SAME EVENING, on the dev_reflow2 hub (no merge driver involved). After hub PR #3 squash-merged, a new branch was cut from main with the hub's already-current export left in the working tree, and export_graph was called on it. It returned `wrote: unchanged`, `chained_from: origin/main@78ea77c`, prev 7b6f3654 (right), and this time it genuinely did not write: the file kept `taken_at: {branch: chore/add-cure-as-a-child, commit: 95e29cd, dirty: true}`, the PREVIOUS branch, while the reply computed the new one. So when only the parent or the tree changed, "unchanged" can mean either "I rewrote it" (the merge case above) or "I left a stale taken_at naming another branch" (this one). Under chg:an-export-says-which-tree-it-was-taken-in that stale file is exactly what the gate refuses to see committed on a branch it was not taken on. Workaround used: move the file aside, export again (`wrote: created`), and the branch and commit came out right. What the three share, as observed and NOT root-caused: each time, the file's prev_content_hash or taken_at was wrong or about to change while content_hash was not, and `wrote: unchanged` came back whether or not the file was rewritten. (2) and (3) disagree on whether a write happened, so no single explanation is offered here; walk it with the root-cause skill before fixing.

RECURRED 2026-09-27, 0.72.0, merging main (#604) into feat/registry-closes-idle-designs (#605). The driver auto-merged docs/design/reflow2.json with prev_content_hash == content_hash (c6aa2bdf…) and no taken_at. The merge commit was pushed before the gate was read, and `reflow2 check` then failed LINEAGE. It was repaired by committing the exporter's own output on top (prev == main's 24345d0a…); the pushed merge commit was not amended.

A lesson for the procedure, not the driver: read the gate BEFORE pushing a merge commit. The known remedy (merge, export, amend the unpushed merge) only works while it is unpushed.

RECURRED 2026-09-29, installed 0.74.0, in a worktree-private store (fix/reflow2-declares-what-settles-intent, PR #628), the export used for a branch's own design records.

1. main (#627) was merged in. The export conflicted, so origin/main's export was checked out, the branch records were re-applied into the private store, and the result was exported with overwrite:true while the merge was still uncommitted. The export therefore chained from the OLD merge-base (prev 4379ed14…). The merge was committed and pushed without reading the gate, and CI failed LINEAGE ("records sha256:4379ed14… where sha256:d3580bc8… is expected"). This is the procedure lesson above, repeated.
2. After the merge commit, export_graph with overwrite:true replied `wrote: unchanged`, `chained_from: origin/main@72917f6`, prev_content_hash d3580bc8… (right). The FILE kept prev 4379ed14…, and the local reflow2_check still failed LINEAGE. So "unchanged" left a stale lineage anchor on disk while the reply computed the correct one. This is case (3) above, now observed for prev_content_hash as well as taken_at.

Workaround that held: delete the file and export again. That gave `wrote: created`, prev d3580bc8…, and the gate passed.

Still not root-caused. The shape stands: when content_hash is unchanged, `wrote: unchanged` can skip rewriting a header whose prev_content_hash or taken_at did change.
